moves.sectionTitle: Comparative explanatory case and motion threshold
moves.currentDescription: Theism raises the probability of consciousness, life-permitting order, moral awareness, and other large-scale features together.
moves.lockedProposition: Theism jointly raises the probability of consciousness, life-permitting order, moral awareness, and other large-scale features.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: just giving you my big idea which is that in my view theism provides a deep and unifying explanation of many things. And so the short idea here is that theism best explains the most. By this I mean that theism raises the probability of many parts of reality. Not just small parts like what you ate for breakfast this morning, but large scale areas of reality such as the existence of consciousness, the existence of a universe in which some life forms could exist somewhere at some time. Uh the sense of right and wrong, and many other areas of reality that are individually and collectively surprising. And I want to make a case that theism makes those areas of of reality more probable than they would otherwise be.

moves.sectionTitle: Comparative explanatory case and motion threshold
moves.currentDescription: Finite creators, multiverses, and unknown explanations remain reasonable competitors to the proposed infinite perfect creator.
moves.lockedProposition: Finite-creator and multiverse hypotheses are reasonable competitors and more likely than an infinite creator; an unknown explanation may be likelier still.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: Uh this is my this is my view, I guess. Basically, um I I see three explanations for the existence of fine-tuning and consciousness and uh the universe as we know it. There's the hypothesis that there's a a creator of the universe, but it's a finite limited being or an imperfect being. There's a hypothesis of an infinite or perfect creator. And then there's the multiverse theory, which is that there are many different universes and only some of them allow for life and consciousness and interesting things happening in them and those are the only ones that anybody ever observes. Okay. Um, I guess my basic view is the finite creator and the multiverse are reasonable theories and they're both more likely than the infinite creator theory. Uh, also by the way, as a side point, I think it's even more likely that there's something else that we haven't thought of. We probably just don't know. Probably nobody has thought of what the correct explanation of the universe is. Um, but since I also am one of these people who hasn't thought of it, I can't say anything more about that.
